headline: KOSPI rebounds 2.2% and KTBs give back part of last week's rally: 10Y +2.6bp to 4.034% even though US 10Y fell 4bp, as the belly leads ahead of Tuesday's CPI
summary: KTBs sold off modestly on the first trading day of November, a payback for last week's 9bp rally with no single local trigger. The belly led: 3Y +2.5bp to 3.740%, 5Y +2.7bp to 3.892% and 10Y +2.6bp to 4.034%, while the 1Y was flat at 3.589% and the 30Y rose only 0.7bp to 4.131%, so 10s30s flattened 2bp to 9.7bp. Money-market rates kept climbing: CD 91-day rose 2bp to 3.34% and CP to 3.81%, both new 1-year highs, and MSB 91-day edged up to 3.188%. Spreads were steady at wide levels: KDB about 28bp over KTB at 1–3Y, AAA bank debentures 45bp over the 1Y KTB and AA- 3Y 69bp over, all in the top tenth of their 1-year ranges except AA- (83rd percentile). The risk-off bid paused rather than reversed.
drivers: KOSPI opened 1.6% lower after the Intel-led US chip rout, then closed up 2.24% at 5,859.08 as institutions bought KRW 1.23tn while foreigners sold KRW 0.37tn. Desks read the bond move as a retracement of last week's rally (3Y −8.8bp, 10Y −8.9bp on the week); the November KTB issuance plan gave little support.
US Treasuries pointed the other way

The US 10Y fell about 4bp on Friday (par 4.98% to 4.94%), which at the 1-year daily beta of 0.46 implied a 1.8bp KTB rally; the 10Y instead rose 2.6bp, so the whole move, about +4.4bp, was local. That narrowed the KTB–UST 10Y gap to −91bp from a 1-year extreme of −97bp (still the 4th percentile).
Record exports and CPI on deck

October exports rose 93.7% y/y to USD 115.3bn with chips up 259%, and Q3 GDP has already beaten. October CPI on Tuesday is expected around 3%; a print at or above that keeps a November BOK hike live, which is why the 2–5Y sector, not the long end, carried the sell-off.
Foreigners bought futures into the dip

Foreign investors net bought 8,813 3Y and 1,998 10Y KTB futures, reversing Friday's selling. On the dashboard's basket valuation fair value fell 8 ticks to 103.61 (3Y) and 29 ticks to 107.84 (10Y); settle prices were not in the wraps we read, so we have no basis read today.
data: +93.7% y/y, USD 115.3bn; chips +259% (p +83.7% revised); surplus USD 42.5bn
Second-highest month on record and on track for USD 1tn this year. It underpins the won, fiscal revenue and the BOK's hawkish lean, but the market is trading AI-capex doubts, not the trade data.
Chip capex and government spending drove a large beat while private consumption fell 0.2%. It keeps front-end hike pricing hard to fade.
Hold at 3.00%, unanimous (after +25bp in July and August)
The Governor guided to staying restrictive; markets lean to 3.25% in November. MSB 91-day at a 1-year high reflects that.
Headline easing, but producer prices point to pass-through; the October print is the swing factor for November.
At or above 3% would cement a hike and lift 2–5Y yields further; below 2.8% would let the front end join the long-end rally.
Pending; a new record surplus is expected
Mostly a won story; little direct impact on KTBs.
view: Today was a pause in a flight-to-quality rally, not a turn: the bond-rally signal is still +1.64, foreigners bought futures, and the move was local payback rather than global (Treasuries rallied). Over four weeks about −20bp of the 10Y's −36bp came from US Treasuries at a weekly beta of 0.58 and −16bp was Korea's own equity-to-bond rotation. With CPI and a possible November hike pinning 1–2Y, I expect the 10Y to hold 3.95–4.15% over the next two weeks, and I still prefer the 3s10s steepener and the 50Y over the 30Y to outright duration. The rotation view is best expressed against Treasuries: hedged with 0.58 × US 10Y, the live signal's rally calls hit 66% and sell-off calls 69% (48% and 57% outright), with a Sharpe of 1.21 against 0.91. KDB remains the place to pick up spread; bank paper and corporates wait until CP–CD stops widening.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y rose 1.4bp to 3.719% (80th percentile of its 1-year range) and the 1Y was flat at 3.589% (88th). With the base rate at 3.00% and MSB 91-day at a 1-year high of 3.188%, the curve still prices about two more hikes, which is consistent with the Q3 GDP beat and record exports. 2s3s at 2bp is the flattest of the year (1st percentile), so the front end is no longer leading rallies.
buckets.call: Unchanged, no trigger hit. Add 2Y above 3.80% or on a sub-2.8% October CPI; fade rallies below 3.62%.

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s is 29.4bp, the 3rd percentile of the year against a 40bp average; the 3Y and 10Y sold off in step today. Our steepener from 29.3bp is open and flat. The long end has room to underperform if KOSPI keeps stabilising, while hike risk caps the front end only so far. One 10Y future carries about 3.0 times the DV01 of a 3Y (KRW 85k vs 29k per bp).
buckets.call: Keep the 3s10s steepener (buy 3 × 3Y, sell 1 × 10Y futures) from 29bp; target 36bp, stop 25bp. Open.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 4.034% sits at the 53rd percentile of a 3.08–4.60% range after a 36bp four-week rally. Today's 2.6bp back-up came against a falling US 10Y, so it was local positioning, not global. The KTB–UST gap of −91bp (4th percentile) says Korea has already outperformed a lot, which limits outright upside from here.
buckets.call: Buy zone 4.10–4.15% not reached; keep it with a stop at 4.25%. Don't chase below 4.00%.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s is +2.4bp, the 94th percentile of the year (average −10bp); the switch from +2.5bp is open. The long end barely moved today (30Y +0.7bp, 50Y +0.6bp) as 10s30s flattened to 9.7bp. Within the long end, off-the-run 2052–53 KTBs trade about 8bp cheap to the fitted curve, while the 2028 bond in the 3Y futures basket is about 7bp rich.
buckets.call: Keep the 30Y into 50Y switch at +2.5bp; target −3bp, stop +6bp. Open.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: The KDB fit (17 trades) puts KDB 28bp over KTB across 1–3Y; at 3Y that is the 92nd percentile against a 19bp average, 2bp wider than our entry. KOFIA's own 1Y KDB quote is 34bp over the KTB (95th percentile, average 23bp). The widening tracks bank funding pressure, not KDB credit.
buckets.call: Hold the overweight from ~26bp; take profit at 20bp, cut above 35bp. Open, 2bp against.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: AAA bank paper (51-trade fit) is 45bp over the 1Y KTB, the widest of the year; CD 91-day rose another 2bp to 3.34% and CP to 3.81%, both 1-year highs, with CP–CD at 47bp (96th percentile). IBK 1Y is 38bp over KTB, also a 1-year wide. Funding pressure is still building into month-start.
buckets.call: No change: prefer KDB over bank debentures; revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls back below 35bp.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y is 69bp over the KTB (83rd percentile, average 60bp) and KEPCO 3Y 44bp over, a 1-year wide (100th percentile). Spreads held as yields rose today, so there is no sign of a turn yet, and one day of equity recovery is not enough to add risk.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI holds its rebound for a week; no trigger hit.

ktb:2.note: Two more hikes priced; CPI Tue

watch: Next: Korea October CPI and the US midterm elections (Tue Nov 3), FX reserves and the US quarterly refunding (Wed Nov 4), Korea September current account (Thu Nov 5), US October payrolls (Fri Nov 6), then the BOK's late-November meeting. A firm CPI with a holding KOSPI rebound is the main risk to the long-end rally; a soft print would let the front end catch up.
sources: Yonhap via Maeil Business (KTB close, Nov 2)
